Oyster Therapeutics · wordmark study

The s as a degrader

A heterobifunctional degrader is two ligands joined by a linker, and a SELFTAC clasps its two halves together at the middle. The s already has that shape: two ends, one spine. Each option below keeps the letter and adds the story by degrees, from a clasp in the spine to a full ring–linker–ring molecule. Shown large, in the new logotype, and at the 42px header size, in Nacre and Tidepool.

Negative-space heads

The two finalists, 08 and F15, with the clasp’s round heads cut out of the letter, one in each half, and the bond between them in the logo’s pearl colour. Rows change the size of the heads; columns move them further from the seam, so further apart. Sizes and distances are fractions of the spine’s thickness, so the two fonts are like for like.

Inset clasp

The letter untouched; the gold clasp sits in the spine, where the two halves of a SELFTAC meet.

02

Clasp gap

The spine is cut square and the halves are held by the clasp: each half keeps its pearl, as in the story.

02a

Clasp gap, longer bond

As 02, with the cut widened so the bond between the two clasp pearls shows clearly: two halves, held apart and joined.

Clasp gap, halves apart

As 02, with each half eased away from the other along the spine, so the letter itself reads as two pieces held by the clasp.

Clasp open

As 02b with the bond left out: the two halves apart, each with its pearl, as when a SELFTAC is split. For contrast with the closed clasp.

Pearl linker

The ends stay as letter (the two ligands); the spine becomes the linker, a strand of pearls with the clasp at its middle.

The serifs become open rings, the generic ligand rings of the 3D story, with the clasp in the spine.

The apple core, and fixes

Cutting the serif s at its thickest point leaves two heavy curved pieces pinched at the middle, and the gold pearls read as pips: from a distance, an apple core. Two ways out: keep the letter’s outline whole and show the halves with a seam, or use a sans s, whose even stroke cuts into two clean hooks.

07

Seam

Newsreader. The outline stays whole; a hairline seam crosses the spine and the clasp straddles it. Two halves, no bite out of the letter.

Header size, 42px
08

Seam, eased apart

Newsreader. The seam opened just enough to see, each half nudged away along the spine; the letter’s outline is nearly intact. The clasp is in the logo’s pearl colour, so the s answers the mark.

Header size, 42px
09

Archivo, halves apart

The Archivo s (the Tidepool logotype’s face) with 02b: an even stroke splits into two hooks rather than two bulbs.

Header size, 42px
10

Archivo, seam

The Archivo s with the seam: the quietest version, the clasp doing all the work.

Header size, 42px

08 in other faces

The same treatment, the seam eased apart with the clasp in the pearl colour, on the s of other faces. Each is drawn from the font’s own outlines, scaled to the height of the current s, and set in the logotype on the font’s default spacing (no kerning or optical spacing yet, which the current logotype has). Serifs first, then sans.
